serialFormats.description: 2010-present: first two digits = year (10 = 2010), digits 3-4 = week of manufacture; 9-13 characters total (typically 10).
sources: PickHVAC — Trane HVAC Age: Serial Number Decoding (https://www.pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/trane/) — '1204' = week 4 of 2012
Parts Town — Trane Serial Number Lookup (https://www.partstown.com/cm/resource-center/guides/gd2/trane-serial-number-lookup)
Inspector Handbook — Decode Trane HVAC Serial Number (https://inspectorhandbook.com/hvac/trane) — serial 2415836472 = week 15 of 2024
Building Intelligence Center — Trane HVAC age (https://www.building-center.org/trane-hvac-age/)
notes: Date portion (YYWW) of the examples is stated by the cited decoders; the trailing characters of examples 1 and 3 are illustrative fillers used only as regex fixtures.

Collision: a 9-character serial made in 2020-2029 (e.g. '2415...') also matches the 2002-2009 one-digit-year rule (2002, week 41). Disambiguate on the nameplate: 2020+ units are R-410A or R-454B (A2L) with Symbio 700/ReliaTel and a modern QR-code plate; 2002-2009 units are R-22 (R-410A only on 2006-2009 designs) with ReliaTel/UCP. Week must be 01-53 under either reading.
No manufacturer document or warranty lookup was available to this builder; confidence capped at medium (two independent secondary decoders agree).

serialFormats.description: 2002-2009: 9-character serial; first digit = last digit of year (2 = 2002 ... 9 = 2009), digits 2-3 = week of manufacture.
sources: PickHVAC — Trane HVAC Age (https://www.pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/trane/) — 'serial starting 752 = built 2007, week 52'; 2002-2009 serials are 9 characters
Building Intelligence Center — Trane HVAC age (https://www.building-center.org/trane-hvac-age/) — format introduced 2002: 1st digit year, 2nd-3rd week
Parts Town — Trane Serial Number Lookup (https://www.partstown.com/cm/resource-center/guides/gd2/trane-serial-number-lookup) — 2002 serials start with 2, 2003 with 3, etc.
notes: Example 1's date prefix '752' is stated by PickHVAC; examples 2 and 3 apply the same rule (year digit + week) with illustrative filler characters — they are regex/rule fixtures, not photographed nameplates.

Collision: a serial starting with 2 could be 2002 or (if the modern 2010+ format) 2020-2029. Real 2002-2009 serials are 9 characters; modern ones are usually 10 or more. If both match, check the refrigerant on the plate (R-22 => 2002-2009) and the model design sequence letter.
One-digit year cannot distinguish 2007 from 1997 by itself, but 1997 serials start with the letter M (see letter-year format), so a leading digit is 2002-2009.

serialFormats.description: 1983-2001: serial begins with a letter = year (W 1983 ... Z 2001), digits 2-3 = week of manufacture; 9 characters typical (8-10 accepted).
sources: Building Intelligence Center — Trane HVAC age (https://www.building-center.org/trane-hvac-age/) — 1983-2001 style: letter = year, positions 2-3 = week
PickHVAC — Trane HVAC Age (https://www.pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/trane/) — W=1983, X=1984, Y=1985, S=1986, B=1987 ... H=1993, J=1994 ... N=1998, P=1999, R=2000; K=1995

H2ouse / How To Look At A House — Trane furnace age (https://www.h2ouse.org/trane-furnace-age/, https://www.howtolookatahouse.com/Blog/Entries/2018/6/how-can-i-tell-the-age-of-a-trane-furnace-from-the-serial-number.html) — S = 1986 and Z = 2001 (out of alphabetical order; easily confused)
notes: K = 1995 (not 1990); 1990 is E. Letters A, I, O, Q, T, U, V are not used in this map.

S and Z are the out-of-order letters: two sources (h2ouse, howtolookatahouse, PickHVAC in one passage) give S = 1986 and Z = 2001; one search summary reversed them (Z = 1986, S = 2001). The pack follows the majority (S = 1986, Z = 2001). If the serial starts with S or Z, confirm with the model design sequence and plate style: 2001 units carry the 'Trane' swoosh-era plate and Voyager/Precedent model numbers; 1986 units are older designs.
Week is the two digits after the letter; a value above 53 means the serial is not this format.
Examples: the year letter and week digits are per the cited charts; the trailing characters are illustrative fillers (no dated nameplate photo was available).

serialFormats.description: 1980-1982 (approximate): the letter in the 3rd position from the end of the serial encodes the year (A/L/O = 1980, B/M/T = 1981, C/N/U = 1982); serial ends with two digits.
sources: PickHVAC — Trane HVAC Age (https://www.pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/trane/) — early-1980s units: letter 3rd from the end = year (A, L & O = 1980 / B, M & T = 1981 / C, N & U = 1982)
notes: LOW CONFIDENCE: only one secondary source describes this style and the overall length/structure of these serials is not documented; the regex is a best guess (ends in two digits, letter third from end). Month position was described as 'the 4th position in some formats' but could not be confirmed, so no month is decoded.
Examples are synthetic fixtures for the regex only. Treat any match as a hint: confirm age from the compressor date code, the nameplate style and the model design sequence.
Pre-1980 Trane serials and the American Standard '4th-position letter' style were not confirmed by any source available to this builder and are not decoded.

controls.description: Microprocessor control on Precedent 3-25 t, Voyager 12.5-25 t (2003+), Voyager III and Odyssey air handlers from about 2003 until replaced by Symbio 700 (2020s). No alphanumeric fault codes: diagnostics are shown by the RTRM green System LED (LED2), by the four LEDs on a zone sensor module (System / Heat / Cool / Service), and by the RTEM LED for the economizer. Full tables: Trane ReliaTel Service & Diagnostics manual (RT-SVD03) and the Trane Commercial Help Center 'List of Light Commercial LED Codes'. Enrichment pass 2026-09-26 by WebSearch only (WebFetch/curl blocked): every meaning is quoted from a search excerpt of the named Trane help-center article, IOM page or the RT-SVD03 diagnostic manual index; likelyCauses/checks combine the source with field practice and say which. Coverage is 'partial': the RT-SVD03 full diagnostic tables (test-mode resistance values, RTDM dehumidification module LEDs, RTAM full table, RTCI/TCI LEDs, Tracer diagnostic names) and the complete Voyager II ReliaTel ignition-board table (codes 3, 4, 6+) were not retrieved; BAYSENS119 codes E0/E6/E7/E8 exist but their meanings were not seen in a credible source (a third-party blog's definitions were generic and were not used). This sidecar supersedes the four 'builder memory / inferred' zone-sensor entries in trane.json (COOL flashing, HEAT flashing, SERVICE steady, SERVICE flashing) with sourced versions using the same code strings, and replaces the single untranscribed 'RTEM LED flashing' entry with

faultCodes.meaning: Normal operation: RTRM powered, no active diagnostic (System output RTRM-J6-9 ON = 'System is powered up. This output should be on whenever the green RTRM System LED is on'). On older-version boards the LED may flicker as part of normal function.

faultCodes.meaning: 'If 0 VDC is seen, the RTRM does not have power, the output wiring is shorted, or there is an internal failure.'
likelyCauses: No 24 VAC to the RTRM (transformer secondary fuse, primary tap, loose power plug)
Shorted low-voltage output wiring pulling the supply down
Failed RTRM
checks: Measure 24 VAC at the RTRM power input; check the transformer secondary fuse and primary tap (field practice)
Measure DC between RTRM J6-6 and J6-9: approximately 32 VDC expected; if no voltage is present with 24 VAC supplied, replace the RTRM (source)
Disconnect low-voltage/zone-sensor wiring to rule out a short (field practice)

(article 360037491092), Table 1 Fail Codes / Table 2 Simultaneous Fail Codes, J6 output definitions

faultCodes.meaning: 'Two Green System LED2 flashes every two seconds indicates one or more diagnostics present. The diagnostic can include fan, sensor, compressor lockout, defrost, gas heat, smoke detector, Frostat, communication, static-pressure, or discharge-air-sensor issues depending on the unit configuration.' The help-center list of possible causes includes: supply fan fail; zone temperature sensor input failure on CV units; programmable ZSM communication failure; manual compressor lockout (one or both circuits); static pressure transducer output failure (VAV only); Frostat active; smoke detector active; RTOM communication failure; RTVM communication failure (22 causes in the full article).
likelyCauses: Supply fan fail (fan proving switch)
Zone temperature sensor input failure on CV units
Programmable ZSM communication failure
Manual compressor lockout, one or both circuits (HPC/LPC/CC circuit trips)
Gas heat failure (see ignition module LED)
Smoke detector active / Frostat active
RTOM or RTVM communication failure
VAV: static pressure transducer or discharge air sensor failure, high duct static trip
checks: Read the specific fail code: take the four DC voltage measurements on RTRM J6 (J6-7 Heat, J6-8 Cool, J6-9 System, J6-10 Service; pulsing = fail) or read the zone sensor LEDs / ZSM display / Tracer (source)
Then follow the matching HEAT FAIL, COOL FAIL, SERVICE or simultaneous-code entry in this table

(article 360037491092), Table 1 Fail Codes / Table 2 Simultaneous Fail Codes, J6 output definitions

faultCodes.meaning: 'Unit is in TEST mode. Also during the TEST mode LED2 will pulse on and off.' (System output J6-9 pulsing = unit in TEST mode.)
checks: Remove the TEST 1 / TEST 2 jumper; a momentary jumper leaves the unit in the selected step for 1 hour before it exits test mode on its own (source)

faultCodes.meaning: Economizer diagnostic present on the ReliaTel Economizer Module; the flash count identifies the fault (actuator, mixed-air/outdoor sensor, enthalpy/CO2 input). Full flash table: Trane help-center article 'LCU Economizer LED Codes (RTEM Module)'.

Economizer actuator not driving / feedback fault
Wiring to RTRM

Check sensor resistance (10k thermistor) and actuator travel in test mode step 'economizer'

faultCodes.notes: Table not transcribed; only the existence and meaning of a flashing RTEM LED is recorded.

faultCodes.meaning: 'Emergency stop open when attempting test mode' (one Green System LED2 blink). Per the Voyager IOM the Emergency Stop input at LTB 5 & 6 (RTRM 3J1-12): if this input is open the indoor fan, heat and cooling will not run in TEST MODE and there is no other diagnostic output for this function.
likelyCauses: Field emergency-stop / fire-alarm contact open
Factory jumper between LTB 5 and 6 removed and no device connected
Broken wire to the E-stop input
checks: Verify continuity between LTB 5 and 6 (jumper or closed field contact)
Check any fire/smoke or BAS shutdown relay wired into the E-stop loop (field practice)

faultCodes.meaning: HEAT FAIL (Heating output RTRM-J6-7 pulsing). 'If any failure occurs such as loss of flame, limit switch trip, flame rollout etc, this indication is present. Further diagnostics are available by examining the Ignition Module LED.' On VAV units with RTAM: HEAT (YC only) = 'Supply Air Temperature sensor has failed if configured for Modulating Heat'. Note: 'If the Compressor Disable circuit or CC1, CC2 circuits create a lockout during heating mode, a COOL FAIL (pulsing) indication will occur, not a HEAT FAIL (pulsing) indication.'
likelyCauses: Ignition module lockout: no flame sensed on ignition or flame dropped out (IGN 2 flash)
Combustion pressure switch not proving (IGN 3 flash)
TCO / high limit open (IGN 4 flash), rollout switch open (IGN 6 flash)
Flame sensed without gas (IGN 5 flash)
VAV modulating heat: supply air temperature sensor failed
checks: Read the ignition module LED flash code (see IGN entries) before touching anything else (source)
Watch a heat call: combustion blower, pressure switch closure, igniter, gas valve, flame sense microamps (field practice)
Check filters, blower, belt and limit switches for a TCO trip (field practice)
Ignition control auto-resets after 1 hour of lockout; cycling the heat call or 24 V power also resets it (source/field practice)

(article 360037491092), Table 1 Fail Codes / Table 2 Simultaneous Fail Codes, J6 output definitions

faultCodes.code: Zone sensor COOL LED on steady
faultCodes.meaning: Cooling output (RTRM-J6-8) 'ON - the system is in the cooling mode and actively cooling. The unit could be economizing or have one or both compressors on.'
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — How do I retrieve fail codes from the RTRM when I have a 2 flash fault code? (article 360037491092), Table 1 Fail Codes / Table 2 Simultaneous Fail Codes, J6 output definitions

faultCodes.meaning: COOL FAIL (Cooling output RTRM-J6-8 pulsing): 'CC1 or CC2 opens during cooling, or is open when a call for compressor occurs. With RTRM version 4.0 or greater, CC1 or CC2 circuit must open on 3 consecutive cycles. On the 4th trip, the unit will lockout.' Also 'If the Compressor Disable circuit or CC1, CC2 circuits create a lockout during heating mode, a COOL FAIL (pulsing) indication will occur.' On VAV units with RTAM: COOL = 'Discharge air sensor (DTS) is open, shorted, or has failed'.
likelyCauses: HPC / temperature discharge limit opened during compressor operation (dirty condenser, ODM failure, overcharge, non-condensables)
LPC opened (loss of charge, low airflow, restricted metering device)
Compressor internal overload, contactor coil or CC1/CC2 24 V circuit open, phase monitor open
Compressor disable input open (BAS or field device)
VAV: discharge air sensor failed
checks: Identify which circuit is locked out (CPR1/CPR2) in test mode and check the HPC, LPC, TDL and CC circuit for 24 V continuity (source + field practice)
Gauge up: verify head and suction pressures, condenser coil condition, ODM operation and compressor amps (field practice)
Reset the manual lockout by cycling 24 V control power or the zone sensor mode switch; on BAS units send the reset from Tracer (field practice)

(article 360037491092), Table 1 Fail Codes / Table 2 Simultaneous Fail Codes, J6 output definitions

faultCodes.meaning: Service output (RTRM-J6-10) 'ON - indicates a clogged filter switch has been closed for at least 2 minutes, indicating a clogged filter.'
likelyCauses: Dirty filters
Clogged filter switch set point too low or sensing tubing pinched/disconnected
checks: Replace filters; verify the clogged filter switch setting and tubing to the RTOM input (source + field practice)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — How do I retrieve fail codes from the RTRM when I have a 2 flash fault code? (article 360037491092), Table 1 Fail Codes / Table 2 Simultaneous Fail Codes, J6 output definitions; Trane TC*150-301 IOM (ManualsLib 959359) p.51 'Clogged Filter Switch; Fan Failure Switch'

faultCodes.meaning: Fan failure: 'The service indicator on the ZSM will pulse during fan fail mode.' 'The Fan Fail switch (if installed) should have opened within the first 40 seconds, proving the supply fan has started; if the Fan Proving switch has failed to open before 40 seconds, the unit will run for 40 seconds and then stop.'
likelyCauses: Broken or slipping belt, seized blower bearing
IDM overload tripped, IFC contactor/relay not pulling in
Fan proving switch stuck or tubing disconnected
VFD fault on VAV / multi-speed units
checks: Call for fan and confirm the IDM runs and the fan proving switch changes state within 40 s (source)
Check belt, motor amps, contactor and the RTOM fan-proving input (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Trane Voyager Commercial IOM (ManualsLib 825268) p.117 'Low Pressure Control (LPC) Sequence of Operation (ReliaTel control); High Pressure Control and Temperature Discharge Limit' and p.132 'Zone Temperature Sensor (ZSM) Service Indicator; RTRM Zone Sensor Module (ZSM) Test'; Trane TC*150-301 IOM (ManualsLib 959359) p.51 'Clogged Filter Switch; Fan Failure Switch'; Trane Commercial Help Center — What can cause a 2 flash code on the RTRM? (article 360038608131)

faultCodes.code: Zone sensor HEAT + COOL LEDs flashing simultaneously
faultCodes.meaning: 'If HEAT FAIL and COOL FAIL occur at the same time (RTRM-J6-7 & 8 pulsing voltage), the coil temperature sensor is open or shorted. Additionally, for heat pump units, the unit may have failed to defrost properly.' (Table 2 Simultaneous Fail Codes.)
likelyCauses: Heat pump coil temperature sensor (CTS) open or shorted, or unplugged from the RTRM
Defrost failure: reversing valve, ODM or CTS location issue
checks: Measure the CTS resistance (10 k NTC thermistor) at the RTRM plug and compare with coil temperature (source + field practice)
Run the defrost step in test mode and confirm the reversing valve shifts and the coil clears (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — List of Light Commercial LED Codes (article 360060172532); Trane Commercial Help Center — How do I retrieve fail codes from the RTRM when I have a 2 flash fault code? (article 360037491092), Table 1 Fail Codes / Table 2 Simultaneous Fail Codes, J6 output definitions

faultCodes.code: Zone sensor COOL + SERVICE LEDs flashing (VAV, RTAM)
faultCodes.meaning: 'COOL + SERVICE: Static Pressure Transducer output voltage at RTAM J1-3 is less than 0.25VDC' (static pressure transducer output failure, VAV only).
likelyCauses: Transducer unplugged or failed
Transducer supply/ground wiring open
checks: Measure DC at RTAM J1-3; expect > 0.25 VDC with the transducer connected (source)
Check transducer pressure tubing and supply voltage (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — List of Light Commercial LED Codes (article 360060172532); Trane Commercial Help Center — What can cause a 2 flash code on the RTRM? (article 360038608131)

faultCodes.code: Zone sensor HEAT + COOL + SERVICE LEDs flashing (VAV, RTAM)
faultCodes.meaning: 'HEAT + COOL + SERVICE: Static Pressure High Duct Static Trip. The static pressure has exceeded 3.5" W.C. three consecutive times' (the Parts Town reproduction adds 'or an open ground wire on the transducer').
likelyCauses: VAV boxes closed / duct dampers shut, fire damper closed
VFD ramped to max on loss of static signal
Transducer ground wire open
checks: Verify duct static with a manometer against the RTAM setpoint (field practice)
Check the transducer ground wire and tubing (source)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — List of Light Commercial LED Codes (article 360060172532); Parts Town 'Trane Rooftop Unit Troubleshooting Guide' (secondary)

faultCodes.code: Zone temperature sensor (ZTS) input failure (CV units)
faultCodes.meaning: 'Zone temperature sensor input failure on CV units' is listed as a cause of the RTRM 2-flash code. Test procedure: 'To test the mechanical zone sensor module temperature inputs at RTRM J6-1 and J6-2, read DC voltage with the sensor attached... With the sensor not attached, there should be 5.00 VDC at the terminals.' Problems to look for include 'mis-wiring, shorts/opens, excessive resistance in the circuit from corroded or loose connections, sensor inaccuracy, moisture in the sensor, and induced voltage from high voltage wires in the same conduit.'
likelyCauses: Open or shorted ZTS thermistor wiring
Corroded/loose terminal connections adding resistance
Moisture in the sensor
Induced voltage from line-voltage wiring in the same conduit
checks: Read DC volts at J6-1/J6-2 with the sensor attached, then ohm the circuit and the sensor itself (source)
If the RTRM loses the heating/cooling setpoint potentiometer input it controls in default mode instantaneously (source)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — What can cause a 2 flash code on the RTRM? (article 360038608131); Trane ReliaTel Microprocessor Controls Diagnostic Manual RT-SVD03G-EN (Nov 2010), as indexed on ManualsLib 2574710 (mechanical zone sensor test)

faultCodes.meaning: 'Programmable ZSM communication failure' is a cause of the RTRM 2-flash code; the Voyager IOM defines it as 'The ZSM has failed to communicate for 15 consecutive minutes after successful communication has occurred.'
likelyCauses: Broken communication wire between the programmable zone sensor and LTB
Failed BAYSENS019/119 sensor
Wrong sensor type configured / wiring landed on wrong terminals
checks: With the wires removed from the control terminals, measure 28-32 VDC between sensor terminals 11 and 12 (source)
Run the unit through test mode to confirm the RTU itself operates; normal display shows time, temperature, fan and system status (source)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — What can cause a 2 flash code on the RTRM? (article 360038608131); Trane Voyager Commercial IOM (ManualsLib 825268) p.117 'Low Pressure Control (LPC) Sequence of Operation (ReliaTel control); High Pressure Control and Temperature Discharge Limit' and p.132 'Zone Temperature Sensor (ZSM) Service Indicator; RTRM Zone Sensor Module (ZSM) Test'; Trane Commercial Help Center — Troubleshooting BAYSENS119 Programmable Zone Sensor (article 5123788263437) and How do I test a Programmable Zone Sensor (BAYSENS119*)? (article 360038266292)

faultCodes.meaning: 'Emergency stop input is open': the Emergency Stop input at LTB 5 & 6 (3J1-12 on RTRM) — 'if this input is open, the indoor fan, heat & cooling will not run in TEST MODE, with no diagnostic output for this function' (other than the single RTRM LED2 blink when test mode is attempted).
likelyCauses: Fire alarm / smoke relay or BAS shutdown contact open
Factory jumper removed
checks: Check continuity across LTB 5-6 and any field device in the loop (source)
faultCodes.source: Trane Voyager Commercial IOM (ManualsLib 825268) emergency-stop description; Trane Commercial Help Center — List of Light Commercial LED Codes (article 360060172532)

faultCodes.meaning: 'Smoke detector active' is a cause of the RTRM 2-flash code; factory-installed smoke detectors provide 'instant shutdown and ICS alarm output'.
likelyCauses: Smoke in return/supply duct
Dirty or failed detector head
Detector power/relay wiring fault
checks: Check the detector's own LED/alarm state and reset it per its manual; verify the shutdown contact wiring to the RTOM/RTRM (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — What can cause a 2 flash code on the RTRM? (article 360038608131); Trane ReliaTel Options Module installation guide ACC-SVN05Q-EN (Trane e-library)

faultCodes.meaning: 'Frostat active' is listed as a cause of the RTRM 2-flash code. The RTOM 'monitors the supply fan proving, clogged filter, supply air temperature, exhaust fan setpoint, supply air tempering, Frostat and smoke detector.' When the Frostat opens (resets) the compressors re-start; the RTOM guide states 'there is no diagnostic during Frostat trip' (the help-center list treats it as a 2-flash cause on later firmware).
likelyCauses: Evaporator coil freezing: low airflow, dirty filters/coil, low charge, low return temperature
checks: Check airflow, filters, blower and refrigerant charge before resetting; the Frostat is wired to the RTOM input (source + field practice)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — What can cause a 2 flash code on the RTRM? (article 360038608131); Trane ReliaTel Options Module installation guide ACC-SVN05Q-EN (Trane e-library)

faultCodes.meaning: 'The RTRM will register an auto reset lockout if either the high pressure control switch or the temperature discharge limit opens during compressor operation. If the compressor output circuit is opened four consecutive times during compressor operation, the RTRM will generate a manual reset lockout.' LPC: 'When the LPC is opened for one (1) continuous second, the compressor for that circuit is turned off immediately. The compressor will not be allowed to restart for a minimum of three (3) minutes. If four consecutive open conditions occur during the first three minutes of operation, the compressor will be locked out, a diagnostic communicated to ICS if applicable, and a manual reset will be required.'
likelyCauses: HPC trips: dirty condenser, ODM failure, overcharge, non-condensables, high ambient
LPC trips: low charge, low evaporator airflow, restricted metering device, frozen coil
TDL (discharge temperature limit) trips: high superheat / low charge
checks: Determine which safety opened (HPC, LPC, TDL) by checking 24 V across each switch during a call (field practice)
Reset the manual lockout by cycling 24 V power / mode switch or via Tracer; fix the cause first (source + field practice)
faultCodes.source: Trane Voyager Commercial IOM (ManualsLib 825268) p.117 'Low Pressure Control (LPC) Sequence of Operation (ReliaTel control); High Pressure Control and Temperature Discharge Limit' and p.132 'Zone Temperature Sensor (ZSM) Service Indicator; RTRM Zone Sensor Module (ZSM) Test'; Trane Commercial Help Center — Low and High Pressure Control (article 12778525483277); Trane Commercial Help Center — What can cause a 2 flash code on the RTRM? (article 360038608131)

faultCodes.code: Compressor proving fault (HPC Lockout / Disable alarm via BAS)
faultCodes.meaning: 'Compressor Proving faults on units with ReliaTel Controls indicates that the RTRM has commanded the compressor contactor on, but the RTRM did not detect that the contactor pulled in or the RTRM detected that the contactor opened while running.' 'Based on the communication interface installed in the unit and the firmware on that interface, the diagnostic can come through in different ways including HPC Lockout or Disable alarms.'
likelyCauses: Open in the CC1/CC2 24 V proving circuit: HPC, LPC, TDL, compressor internal overload, contactor coil
Phase monitor open
Compressor disable input open
checks: Check 24 V at the contactor coil and through each series safety while the RTRM calls for the compressor (source + field practice)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — Compressor Proving on ReliaTel Controlled Units (article 42150055236109)

faultCodes.meaning: 'RTVM communication failure' is a cause of the RTRM 2-flash code; on the RTVM the green system LED at '1/4 second on, 2 seconds off' means 'No communication'.
likelyCauses: Communication harness unplugged
Failed RTVM or RTRM port
checks: Check the RTVM LED pattern and the harness to the RTRM (source)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — What can cause a 2 flash code on the RTRM? (article 360038608131); Trane Commercial Help Center — List of Light Commercial LED Codes (article 360060172532)

faultCodes.meaning: 'Heat failure indicates an error in the heating system... On the display, error codes toggle with the clock' (BAYSENS019/119 programmable zone sensor).
checks: Same diagnosis as 'Zone sensor HEAT LED flashing': read the ignition module LED
faultCodes.source: Trane ReliaTel Microprocessor Controls Diagnostic Manual RT-SVD03G-EN (Nov 2010), as indexed on ManualsLib 2574710 p.81 'Programmable Zone Sensor BAYSENS119A and BAYSENS019C'

faultCodes.meaning: 'Cool failure indicates an error in the cooling system... On the display, error codes toggle with the clock.' Note from the BAYSENS119 troubleshooting article: the sensor may falsely report a cooling failure when there is no cooling call if sensor wiring/communication to the RTU is faulty — verify wiring and communication.
checks: Same diagnosis as 'Zone sensor COOL LED flashing'; verify sensor wiring/communication first if there was no cooling demand (source)
faultCodes.source: Trane ReliaTel Microprocessor Controls Diagnostic Manual RT-SVD03G-EN (Nov 2010), as indexed on ManualsLib 2574710 p.81; Trane Commercial Help Center — Troubleshooting BAYSENS119 Programmable Zone Sensor (article 5123788263437) and How do I test a Programmable Zone Sensor (BAYSENS119*)? (article 360038266292)

faultCodes.code: RTEM LED blink: off 2 s, on 1/4 s (1/2 s on, 2 s off)
faultCodes.meaning: Communications failure with the RTRM: 'BLINK Communications Failure is LED OFF for 2 seconds, then LED ON for 1/4 second' (the LED-code list words the no-communication pattern as '1/2 second on, 2 seconds off'). Distinguish from the 1-flash actuator fault, which is 'LED ON for 2 seconds, then LED OFF for 1/4 second'.
likelyCauses: Harness between RTEM and RTRM unplugged/damaged
Failed RTEM or RTRM
checks: Watch whether the LED is mostly off (comm failure) or mostly on (actuator fault) (source)
Reseat the RTRM-RTEM harness; cycle 24 V (field practice)

faultCodes.meaning: Error code (1/2 second on, 1/4 second off per flash): Actuator fault ('1 Flash Actuator Fault is LED ON for 2 seconds, then LED OFF for 1/4 second')
likelyCauses: Economizer actuator not driving or no feedback
Actuator wiring/plug
Damper linkage bound
checks: Drive the damper in the economizer test-mode step and watch travel and feedback (field practice)
Check the actuator plug and wiring at the RTEM (source)

checks: Check the CO2 sensor output/supply at the RTEM input (field practice)

checks: Check the RA humidity sensor signal at the RTEM (field practice)

checks: Ohm the RAT thermistor at the RTEM plug (field practice)

checks: Check the OA humidity sensor signal at the RTEM (field practice)

likelyCauses: Outdoor air temperature sensor open/shorted
RTRM communication lost
checks: Ohm the OAT sensor; check the RTEM-RTRM harness (source)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — LCU Economizer LED Codes (RTEM Module) (article 360037863611) and What are the Economizer fault codes? (article 360060609671)

faultCodes.meaning: Error code (1/2 second on, 1/4 second off per flash): MA temp sensor
likelyCauses: Mixed air sensor open/shorted or not installed

'Pull the two pin plug from the MAT inputs on the RTEM and measure resistance across the two pins; if you read open or short, replace the mixed air sensor.' (source)

likelyCauses: RTEM board failure
checks: Cycle power; if the code persists replace the RTEM (field practice)

faultCodes.meaning: 'If LED1 is out, this indicates that there is no power to the ignition module.'
likelyCauses: No 24 V / heat transformer power to the ignition module
Ignition board failed
Board unresponsive after RTRM replacement (help-center article 4459483187341)
checks: Check power at the ignition module plug; if the RTRM was just replaced, see article 4459483187341 (source)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — What are the gas heat fault codes for Precedent units? (article 360038604571) and Precedent Electromechanical Ignition Board Info and Troubleshooting Tips (article 360043948432)

faultCodes.code: IGN LED1 solid green / slow pulse (Precedent ignition module)
faultCodes.meaning: 'The ignition module LED1 will be solid green with no heat call and in a slow pulse (3/4 sec on, 1/4 sec off) for a heating call, and will also blink codes (1/4 sec on, 1/4 sec off with a 2 sec pause at the end of the code) for diagnostics.' On the CNT05135 electromechanical board (two LEDs, Status and Fault): Status 'Slow Flash indicates normal operation with a cool or fan only call; Fast Flash indicates normal operation with a call for heat only.'
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — What are the gas heat fault codes for Precedent units? (article 360038604571) and Precedent Electromechanical Ignition Board Info and Troubleshooting Tips (article 360043948432)

faultCodes.meaning: '1 Hour Lockout' — 'A 2 flash diagnostic indicates that either no flame was sensed on ignition or that the flame dropped out while running.' 'The ignition control will reset automatically after 1 hour in Lock-up mode.'
likelyCauses: No gas / gas valve not opening
Dirty or cracked flame sensor, poor flame-sense ground
Igniter failed, poor burner carry-over
Flue/combustion air problem causing flame dropout
checks: Watch an ignition trial for spark/HSI, gas valve voltage and flame; measure flame-sense microamps (field practice)
Reset by cycling the heat call / 24 V power, or wait 1 hour (source)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — What are the gas heat fault codes for Precedent units? (article 360038604571) and Precedent Electromechanical Ignition Board Info and Troubleshooting Tips (article 360043948432)

faultCodes.meaning: 'Pressure Switch' — 'the pressure switch did not close in the correct amount of time after the combustion fan was energized, opened while the unit was heating or is closed when the combustion fan is commanded off.'
likelyCauses: Restricted, pulled loose or leaking pressure switch hose; flue box hose fitting restricted with debris or rust
Combustion blower not running or slow
Blocked flue / vent
Switch stuck closed
checks: Confirm the combustion blower runs; check hose and flue-box fitting; measure inches w.c. at the switch (source + field practice)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — What are the gas heat fault codes for Precedent units? (article 360038604571) and Precedent Electromechanical Ignition Board Info and Troubleshooting Tips (article 360043948432)

faultCodes.meaning: 'TCO Open' (high temperature limit / thermal cut-out open).
likelyCauses: Low airflow: dirty filters, belt, blower, closed dampers
Over-fired heat exchanger
Failed TCO
checks: Check temperature rise, filters and blower; ohm the TCO when cool (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — What are the gas heat fault codes for Precedent units? (article 360038604571) and Precedent Electromechanical Ignition Board Info and Troubleshooting Tips (article 360043948432)

faultCodes.meaning: 'Flame W/O Gas' — 'the ignition module is sensing a flame without a call for heat. This could be a failing flame sensor or a gas valve that is not closing.' 'If there is a (5) flash code and the indoor fan is not on, it is a bad board. If there is a (5) Flash code and there is no flame present, it is a bad board.'
likelyCauses: Gas valve leaking through / not closing
Flame sensor or its wiring shorted
Ignition board failed
checks: Look for flame with the gas valve de-energized; if none and the fan is off, replace the board (source)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — What are the gas heat fault codes for Precedent units? (article 360038604571) and Precedent Electromechanical Ignition Board Info and Troubleshooting Tips (article 360043948432)

faultCodes.meaning: 'Rollout Switch Open'.
likelyCauses: Flame rollout from a blocked heat exchanger, flue or dirty burners
Manual-reset rollout switch tripped
checks: Inspect the heat exchanger, burners and flue for blockage before resetting the rollout switch (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — What are the gas heat fault codes for Precedent units? (article 360038604571) and Precedent Electromechanical Ignition Board Info and Troubleshooting Tips (article 360043948432)

faultCodes.meaning: 'W1 / W2 Sw' (W1/W2 input switch diagnostic). Note: 'A W1 & W2 simultaneous call (such as W1 and W2 jumped together) gives you Low Fire for 10 minutes before transitioning to High Fire' and 'you do not need a G call with a W1 call (the board will automatically turn on the fan 45 seconds after proving flame).'
likelyCauses: W2 present without W1 / miswired heat stages
RTRM heat outputs or wiring to the ignition board
checks: Verify W1 and W2 24 V signals at the ignition board during a heat call (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — What are the gas heat fault codes for Precedent units? (article 360038604571) and Precedent Electromechanical Ignition Board Info and Troubleshooting Tips (article 360043948432)

faultCodes.code: Voyager II IGN LED ON / slow flash / fast flash

faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — What are the gas heat fault codes for Reliatel controlled Voyager II units? (article 360038605131); Star Supply reproduction 'Ignition Troubleshooting Codes, ReliaTel-Electromechanical'

faultCodes.meaning: 'Communications Lockup'.
likelyCauses: Loss of communication between the ignition board and the RTRM
checks: Check the harness between the RTRM and ignition board; cycle 24 V (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — What are the gas heat fault codes for Reliatel controlled Voyager II units? (article 360038605131); Star Supply reproduction 'Ignition Troubleshooting Codes, ReliaTel-Electromechanical'

faultCodes.meaning: 'System Lockout'. 'The ignition control will reset automatically after 1 hour in Lock-up mode.'

Pressure switch, limit or rollout trips ending in lockout

faultCodes.meaning: 'Flame sensed without gas valve energized'.
likelyCauses: Gas valve not closing
Flame sensor circuit shorted
Ignition board failed
checks: Confirm no flame with the valve de-energized; check the flame-sense wiring (field practice)

diagnosticTips: TEST mode: momentarily short the TEST 1 and TEST 2 terminals on the low-voltage terminal board (LTB) for 2-3 seconds and remove the short; the unit enters step 1 (indoor fan). Each further momentary short advances one step (economizer, cool 1, cool 2, heat 1, heat 2 ... per unit configuration); holding the short in continuously auto-advances the steps. The unit leaves test mode about one hour after entry (per the UCP/ReliaTel IOM test-mode description). RTRM LED2 pulses while in test.
LEDs: RTRM System LED2 is on the RTRM board in the control box; zone sensor LEDs (System/Heat/Cool/Service) are on BAYSENS zone sensors that have LEDs.

Clearing lockouts: compressor and heat lockouts clear by cycling 24 V control power (open the unit disconnect for ~10 s) or by switching the zone sensor / thermostat mode to OFF and back; on BAS-connected units send the reset from Tracer.

Zone sensor input is a 10 kohm thermistor; an open or shorted ZTS gives a sensor-failure diagnostic (2-flash on LED2) and the RTRM falls back per its configuration. Check resistance at LTB before replacing the RTRM.
Full LED and diagnostic tables: Trane ReliaTel Service & Diagnostics Manual (RT-SVD03), ReliaTel user guide CNT-SVX15D-E4, and support.trane.com 'List of Light Commercial LED Codes'.

TEST MODE (auto-cycle): place a jumper from TEST 1 to TEST 2 on the Low Voltage Terminal Board (LTB). The unit runs each mode for 30 seconds, scrolling through all modes relevant to that model, then exits test mode automatically; to run it again remove the jumper for ~2 seconds and restore it. Stages: Supply Fan On, Economizer open and close, Cool 1, Cool 2, Heat 1, Heat 2, Emergency Heat (heat pumps only), Outdoor Coil Defrost (heat pump only); a stage is skipped if the unit lacks that component. (help-center 360060176192 / 360037863991)

TEST MODE (step / hold): if the jumper is removed at any time during test mode the unit stays in the currently selected mode for 1 hour (except defrost on heat pumps), then exits and resumes normal operation. Specific operating states can also be selected by applying the appropriate resistance from TEST 1 to TEST 2, in any order (RT-SVD03 resistance table not transcribed). RTRM LED2 and the ZSM SYSTEM indicator pulse while in test mode. If the Emergency Stop input (LTB 5-6) is open nothing will run in test mode and LED2 gives one blink.

READING A 2-FLASH: take four DC voltage measurements on the RTRM J6 connector (J6-7 Heat, J6-8 Cool, J6-9 System, J6-10 Service; measure to J6-6): steady voltage = that mode is ON, pulsing voltage = FAIL. Table 1 'Fail Codes' and Table 2 'Simultaneous Fail Codes' in help-center article 360037491092 map single and combined pulsing outputs (HEAT, COOL, SERVICE, HEAT+COOL, COOL+SERVICE, HEAT+COOL+SERVICE) to the entries in this table. About 32 VDC between J6-6 and J6-9 is expected; if absent, replace the RTRM.

WHERE THE LEDS ARE: RTRM System LED2 is on the RTRM in the unit control box; the RTEM (economizer) and RTVM (ventilation) LEDs are on their own modules; the ignition module LED1 is on the ignition board in the gas heat section; zone sensor SYSTEM/HEAT/COOL/SERVICE LEDs are on BAYSENS zone sensors that have indicators (driven from RTRM J6-7/8/9/10); programmable sensors (BAYSENS019/119) show HEAT FAIL / COOL FAIL text toggling with the clock (BAYSENS119 also E1/E2). On BAS units the same diagnostics reach Tracer through the RTCI/TCI (compressor proving may show as 'HPC Lockout' or 'Disable' depending on the interface firmware).

ZONE SENSOR TEST: mechanical ZSM temperature input at RTRM J6-1/J6-2 reads 5.00 VDC with the sensor disconnected; with it attached read DC volts, then ohm the circuit and the thermistor. Programmable ZSM: with control wires removed, 28-32 VDC between sensor terminals 11 and 12; run the unit through test mode to prove the RTU before condemning the sensor.

CLEARING LOCKOUTS: compressor manual-reset lockouts (4 consecutive HPC/TDL/LPC/CC-circuit trips) and ignition lockouts clear by cycling 24 V control power (or the zone sensor / thermostat mode switch to OFF and back); the ignition control also auto-resets after 1 hour; on BAS units send the reset from Tracer. Fix the cause first: the RTRM v4.0+ counts consecutive trips.

RTEM 8-FLASH: on units with a 0-50% motorized outdoor-air damper (no economizer) there is no mixed-air sensor and the 8 flash code is ignored; on economizer units pull the MAT two-pin plug and ohm the sensor (open/short = replace).
RTEM ACTUATOR FAULT vs COMM FAILURE: 1-flash actuator fault = LED on 2 s / off 1/4 s; communications failure = LED off 2 s / on 1/4 s.

sequenceOfOperation: Cooling (ReliaTel): on Y1/zone-sensor cooling demand the RTRM starts the IDM (immediately or per fan mode), then — if an RTEM economizer is fitted and outdoor conditions are suitable — modulates the economizer first; when the economizer cannot satisfy the load, the RTRM closes CC1 to start CPR1 (and ODM) after the minimum off-timer; Y2 / further demand brings on CPR2 via CC2. HPC/LPC trips are counted per cooling cycle; repeated trips lock out that compressor until reset.

Heating (gas, ReliaTel): on W1 the RTRM energizes the ignition control (IGN); the combustion blower (CBM) starts and the pressure switch must prove; after prepurge the igniter sparks and the gas valve (GV) opens; flame sensor (FS) must prove within the trial time or IGN retries then locks out (heat-failure diagnostic). Indoor fan starts after the heat fan-on delay; TCO limits open the ignition circuit on overtemperature. W2 stages the second heat stage / high fire.
Heat pump: RTRM energizes the reversing valve solenoid in the cooling mode (Trane 'O' logic), defrost by demand/time via the defrost control; electric heat staged via W1/W2 with the compressor.

Ventilation / economizer: RTEM drives the economizer actuator to minimum position when the fan runs occupied; free cooling enabled by dry-bulb or enthalpy (OHS) comparison; CO2 demand-controlled ventilation via RTVM when fitted.
notes: Designators CPR, CC, ODM, IDM, TNS, HPC, LPC are transcribed from the legend of Trane wiring diagram 1213-4333 (Trane eLibrary); the remaining designators are from builder memory of the Precedent ReliaTel wiring manual and must be confirmed against the diagram printed on the unit (drawing number on the control-box door).

3-phase scroll compressors on 208-230/460/575 V units are rotation-sensitive: verify rotation at start-up (suction/discharge pressures, noise); Trane fits a phase monitor on many 3-phase ReliaTel/Symbio units — check for a 'PM' / phase-monitor relay on the diagram before assuming.

Symbio 700 units: the controller replaces RTRM/RTOM/RTEM functions on one board with expansion modules; thermostat interface is via the Symbio 700 low-voltage terminals (R/G/Y1/Y2/W1/W2) or zone sensor; BACnet MS/TP directly on the controller.

likelyCauses: Low charge from leaks (LPC trips)
Dirty condenser or failed ODM (HPC trips)
Compressor contactor or internal overload
Phase loss or reverse rotation on 3-phase scroll
checks: Pressures and superheat/subcooling per circuit
ODM operation and condenser cleanliness
CC coil voltage and contacts, compressor amps vs RLA
Reset by cycling 24 V power and observe the next trip

commonIssues.symptom: Gas heat will not light or locks out intermittently (Heat LED flashing)
likelyCauses: Dirty/cracked flame sensor rod (low microamps)
Combustion pressure switch not closing (blocked flue/inducer, cracked tubing)
Gas pressure low / regulator
Igniter failed
High-limit TCO tripping on low airflow (dirty filters, belt slip)
checks: Watch a full ignition trial in test mode heat step
Flame current, manifold pressure, pressure-switch differential
Filters, belt tension and blower amps
sources: Builder field-pattern summary; ignition sequence per ReliaTel gas/electric IOM RT-SVX21

Fan proving switch or tubing

Motor amps and bearing noise
Fan proving switch closure with fan running
VFD fault log

Check the overflow switch and reset
